title: How to run a freight brokerage through a slow market.
seoTitle: How to run a freight brokerage through a slow market
searchIntent: What should freight brokers focus on when demand slows?
excerpt: Review customer demand, operating costs, and sales activity without treating historical market forecasts as current guidance.
takeaway: Follow the customer’s actual demand, keep spending purposeful, and continue developing relationships while protecting current service.

sections.title: Avoid treating logistics as automatically recession-proof.
paragraphs: Luis’s slow-market discussions recognize that freight continues to move while particular industries and customers can change sharply. The existence of transportation demand does not mean every brokerage or customer portfolio is protected from a downturn.

Start with the business you actually serve. Review shipment activity and speak to customers about what has changed. A headline about rates may not explain whether one account is facing seasonal demand, a production change, or a service problem that has moved freight elsewhere.

sections.title: Look at the inputs behind changing demand.
paragraphs: The lesson uses a historical pandemic example: the brokerage’s liquid-bulk capability was relevant to increased alcohol movement associated with hand sanitizer. The example illustrates looking at the materials behind a growing product, not a current recommendation to pursue that commodity.

Ask which products are moving and which inputs those products require. This can reveal adjacent businesses and transportation needs. Treat the answer as research to verify with actual prospects rather than assuming a widely discussed trend will create suitable work for your company.

sections.title: Develop capability deliberately.
paragraphs: Luis argues against becoming so narrow that the brokerage cannot recognize changing requirements. That is different from rejecting expertise or a clear market position. Knowing freight brokerage well and developing a particular capability can help you understand adjacent work.

Do not respond to a slow market by promising unfamiliar service without preparation. Evaluate the requirements, providers, and responsibilities first. The objective is useful flexibility supported by knowledge, not adding every mode to a list because the current workload has declined.

sections.title: Keep the operation appropriately lean.
paragraphs: The source asks the owner to understand the purpose of each expense. Review software, marketing, and staffing against the work they support. Anxiety about the market can make a new purchase feel like action even when its operating purpose is unclear.

Improve visibility and repeatable processes before hiring ahead of demand. At the same time, distinguish unnecessary costs from the work needed to protect customer service and carrier payment. Cutting a control that prevents problems may be a poor way to reduce the expense of a slow period.

sections.title: Continue outreach and reactivate relationships.
paragraphs: The dated update video adds a countercyclical sales theme: contact old customers, follow up, and seek appropriate quote or bid opportunities instead of coasting because business feels slow. The point is to keep learning about current customer needs.

That work should remain specific. Ask about a changed operation, upcoming freight, or a relevant opportunity. A slower period does not make a generic message more valuable. Use available capacity to improve research and continuity with contacts who have already engaged.

sections.title: Keep historical commentary in its period.
paragraphs: One source explicitly discusses what was coming in 2023. This article uses the operating lessons from that discussion without presenting its forecasts, promised tools, or program announcements as current facts or offers.

The enduring priorities are purposeful spending, reliable execution, and continued customer development. Review those priorities against the business you have now. A historical market story can suggest questions, but current decisions need current information from your customers and operation.
